provenance: Awakening from the Meaning Crisis Ep. 45
source_note_title: Episode 45: Awakening from the Meaning Crisis - The Nature of Wisdom
translation: The cultivated ability to realize what matters, see through self-deception, and respond well to complex life situations in a way that deepens truth, meaning, and transformation.
origin_background: Wisdom is one of the oldest philosophical and religious ideals, but in Vervaeke's work it is also treated as a legitimate target of cognitive science and psychology rather than as mere moral decoration or inspirational vagueness.
vervaeke_usage: Vervaeke uses wisdom as the central integrative aim of his project: not just intelligence or knowledge, but the optimization of cognition and character toward reality-contact, reduced self-deception, and meaningful self-transcendence.

provenance: Awakening from the Meaning Crisis Ep. 44
source_note_title: Episode 44: Awakening from the Meaning Crisis - Theories of Wisdom
translation: Real in the relation between agent and world rather than existing only inside the subject or only inside the object.
origin_background: The term is a Vervaeke-style extension beyond the usual subjective/objective split. It is used to name fitting, meaning, and intelligibility as relational achievements rather than private projections or brute object-properties.
vervaeke_usage: Vervaeke uses transjective language to explain why meaning, problem-solving, and wisdom are not merely subjective feelings or objective facts. They emerge in the fit between self and world, where relevance is realized.
notes: Promoted from user-curated k4 row in the POD extraction sheet.

provenance: Awakening from the Meaning Crisis Ep. 13
source_note_title: Episode 13: Awakening from the Meaning Crisis - Buddhism and Parasitic Processing
translation: A self-undermining pattern in which the mind's problem-solving and salience machinery gets hijacked into loops that feed anxiety, craving, self-deception, and loss of agency.
origin_background: The phrase sits at the intersection of Buddhist insight, cognitive science, and psychopathology. It names a process where adaptive intelligence becomes trapped in maladaptive recursive loops.
vervaeke_usage: Vervaeke uses parasitic processing to explain how relevance realization can turn against itself, producing compulsive narrowing, addiction-like reinforcement, and existential distortion instead of wisdom.
notes: Promoted from user-curated k4 row in the POD extraction sheet. Existing corpus also has a combined entry 'Reciprocal narrowing / parasitic processing'; this adds the standalone search term.

provenance: Awakening from the Meaning Crisis Ep. 10
translation: A possibility for action that the world offers to a suitably skilled and situated agent.
origin_background: The concept comes from ecological psychology, especially J. J. Gibson, and was later taken up in embodied and enactive cognition to show that perception is already action-oriented rather than a neutral inner picture of the world.
vervaeke_usage: Vervaeke uses affordances to explain how relevance realization couples cognition to the world: we do not first build a detached model and then act, but directly pick up what the world affords us as agents.
notes: Promoted from user-curated k4 row in the POD extraction sheet.

source_note_title: Why You Need An Ecology of Practices
translation: A set of complementary practices that correct, challenge, and strengthen one another so that transformation is sustainable instead of one-sided or self-deceptive.
origin_background: The phrase draws on ecological thinking and practice theory: the point is that no single technique is enough. Different practices form a living system of checks, balances, and mutual enhancement.
vervaeke_usage: Vervaeke uses an ecology of practices as the practical answer to the meaning crisis: meditation, contemplation, dialogos, movement, reading, and other disciplines should work together so that growth is real rather than performative or lopsided.
notes: Promoted from user-curated k4 row in the POD extraction sheet.

source_note_title: Meditating with John Vervaeke - Lesson 11: Lectio Divina
translation: A contemplative way of reading in which a text is not mined just for information but engaged so that it can reshape attention, understanding, and being.
origin_background: Lectio divina is a traditional Christian monastic practice built around slow, prayerful, transformative reading rather than fast information extraction.
vervaeke_usage: Vervaeke uses lectio divina as an example of reading as spiritual-cognitive practice: the point is to let the text 'read you' and participate in transformation, not merely to accumulate propositions.
notes: Promoted from user-curated k4 row in the POD extraction sheet.

source_note_title: John Vervaeke, Circling, and Authentic Relating
translation: An interpersonal practice of deep real-time attention in which people track present-moment experience, relationship, and mutual disclosure to increase contact with what is actually happening between them.
origin_background: Circling comes out of the authentic relating world, especially work associated with Guy Sengstock and related communities. It is not originally a Vervaeke coinage, but it intersects strongly with dialogos, participatory knowing, and collective transformation.
vervaeke_usage: Vervaeke treats circling as one of the contemporary practices that can cultivate dialogical presence, reciprocal opening, and deeper contact with self, other, and shared intelligibility.
notes: Promoted from user-curated k4 row in the POD extraction sheet. Translation seed hint: from Guy Senstock. Marked provisional because the accessible grounding used here is a secondary Circling/Vervaeke source rather than a primary transcript page.

source_note_title: POD sheet continuity / existing Meta Crisis entry
translation: A crisis made of many crises that interact with and intensify one another instead of staying isolated.
origin_background: The term is contemporary and increasingly used for interlocking ecological, social, political, technological, and existential breakdowns rather than a single failure point.
vervaeke_usage: Vervaeke uses the meta-crisis frame to show that modern breakdowns are mutually amplifying and cannot be solved piecemeal without a deeper recovery of wisdom and collective transformation.
notes: Promoted from user-curated k4 row in the POD extraction sheet. Standalone hyphenated form added because existing corpus had 'Meta Crisis' as the unhyphenated variant.

translation: An expanded embodied view of mind in which cognition is not just in the brain but enacted across body, world, culture, tools, and developmental participation in living systems of meaning.
origin_background: The better-known label is 4E cognition—embodied, embedded, enacted, extended. '6E' is a later expanded shorthand used in Vervaeke-adjacent contexts to capture a richer, more participatory and ecological account of mind.
vervaeke_usage: Vervaeke uses expanded E-cognition frameworks to resist brain-bound and purely representational pictures of intelligence. The point is that meaning and mind arise through agent-arena coupling, sociality, practice, and transformation, not isolated symbol manipulation.
notes: Promoted from user-curated k4 row in the POD extraction sheet. Reference hint in sheet pointed to Antoine Buteau summary. Marked provisional because the accessible grounding here is a secondary synthesis source and the exact 6E label is looser than core 4E usage.

provenance: Awakening from the Meaning Crisis Ep. 10
translation: The organized field of what stands out to you as important, relevant, urgent, attractive, dangerous, or worth acting on.
origin_background: The metaphor joins ecological and phenomenological ideas about attention, action, and world-disclosure. It treats relevance not as a single spotlight but as a structured landscape of prominence and pull.
vervaeke_usage: Vervaeke uses salience landscape to explain how consciousness and relevance realization shape experience before explicit thought. Transformation changes not just beliefs but what shows up as real, pressing, and meaningful in the first place.
notes: Promoted from user-curated k4 row in the POD extraction sheet.

provenance: Awakening from the Meaning Crisis Ep. 16
source_note_title: Episode 16: Awakening from the Meaning Crisis - Christianity and Agape
translation: A fundamental turning of the mind and self in which your whole orientation, attention, and way of being are reconfigured.
origin_background: The Greek word metanoia has deep religious and philosophical history, especially in Christian contexts where it is often translated as repentance, but more deeply means a radical transformation of understanding and orientation.
vervaeke_usage: Vervaeke uses metanoia for the deep reorientation brought about by transformative insight, agapic love, and awakening: not merely changing an opinion, but changing the salience-structuring machinery of the self.
notes: Promoted from user-curated k4 row in the POD extraction sheet. Standalone form added because existing corpus had only 'Metanoia / metanoetic passage'.

provenance: Awakening from the Meaning Crisis Ep. 31
source_note_title: Episode 31: Embodied-Embedded RR as Dynamical-Developmental GI
translation: Becoming too narrowly adapted to a limited pattern or dataset so that apparent success in one context produces brittleness, bias, and poor general fit in the wider world.
origin_background: The term comes from statistics and machine learning, where a model can fit its training data so tightly that it fails to generalize. Vervaeke borrows it as a useful analogy for cognition and adaptive behavior.
vervaeke_usage: Vervaeke uses overfitting to show why intelligence needs flexibility, resilience, and relevance realization rather than narrow optimization. Minds can lock into local success patterns that distort broader reality-contact.
notes: Promoted from user-curated k4 row in the POD extraction sheet. Translation seed hint: probably RR related.
